<a id="20261006233728"></a>

## Design-rationale literature, as evidence for an argument scheme

*2026-10-06 23:37:28 · curation · record*

The owner is considering extending this record with argument-development
schemes: questions, claims and objections, in the manner of IBIS. Systems
of that kind have a fifty-year history, and most of it is a history of
not being used. The owner asked for that literature to be held here, as
the cautionary evidence the extension should be weighed against. The
failure modes it documents are these:

- the cost of capture falls on the author while the benefit goes to a
  later reader;
- users will not commit early to a formal structure;
- explicit structure has a cognitive overhead.

## What entered

Nine works, all registered and none read, so none has a NOTE ([ADR-025](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-025.md)):

- the notations and tools: Kunz and Rittel's 1970 working paper that
  introduced IBIS ([LIT-758](../../record/literature.d/LIT-758.md)), gIBIS ([LIT-762](../../record/literature.d/LIT-762.md)) and QOC
  ([LIT-763](../../record/literature.d/LIT-763.md));
- the success case: Conklin and Burgess Yakemovic's field trial, where an
  indented-text IBIS captured more than 2,300 decisions ([LIT-755](../../record/literature.d/LIT-755.md));
- the failure modes: Grudin on who does the work and who benefits
  ([LIT-759](../../record/literature.d/LIT-759.md), [LIT-757](../../record/literature.d/LIT-757.md)), Buckingham Shum and Hammond on what
  argumentation-based rationale is for and what it costs ([LIT-761](../../record/literature.d/LIT-761.md)),
  Lee's seven practical issues ([LIT-760](../../record/literature.d/LIT-760.md)), and Shipman and Marshall
  on why users will not formalize ([LIT-756](../../record/literature.d/LIT-756.md)).

The owner's list had eight. I added Conklin and Burgess Yakemovic,
because a body of failure evidence needs the case that did not fail, and
its abstract says what made the difference: capture with little
disruption of the normal process. I considered Grudin's chapter
"Evaluating opportunities for design capture" in Moran and Carroll's
*Design Rationale* (1996), and left it out: the only DOI is the 2020
reissue's, and the 1996 first appearance could not be dated from a
source.

No topic held these works, so `design-rationale` joins the topics
([ADR-030](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-030.md)). They are not anthology material. None is about machine
learning, and the anthology's nearest topic, `human-ai-interaction`, is
about working with a model. A grep of the anthology's record for every
author and DOI found nothing.

## How deeply

Every bibliographic detail was checked against Crossref, and the dates
follow [ADR-002](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md). What the entries say about content comes from abstracts.
For Kunz and Rittel, the abstract came from the eScholarship scan, whose
title page was seen. For Grudin 1988, Buckingham Shum and Hammond, and
Shipman and Marshall, publishers refused this client. Their takeaways
come from secondary descriptions of the abstract, or, for Shipman and
Marshall, from an outline of the authors' web version, and each entry
says so. Two dates need a word:

- Grudin 1988 takes the CSCW '88 opening day, because Crossref gives
  the paper only a year.
- Grudin 1994 takes 2 January 1994, which is the date Crossref gives.

## What a reading should check

Whether the record's own experience bears out the first failure mode.
Here the person filing an entry is usually also its later reader, which
is the condition Grudin's argument says is missing. Buckingham Shum and
Hammond, and the Conklin and Burgess Yakemovic field trial, are the
places to look for whether that changes the cost-and-benefit balance.

<a id="20261007010616"></a>

## Four works cited by The Organization of Will

*2026-10-07 01:06:16 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-805 — Deferred: registered unread, filed in this entry -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-787 — Deferred: registered unread, filed in this entry -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-817 — Deferred: registered unread, filed in this entry -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-832 — Deferred: registered unread, filed in this entry -->

The owner's essay "The Organization of Will" cites four works the record
did not hold. They entered because the essay cites them, and because the
record of the essay's argument, being built alongside it, needs something
to point at when a step of the argument leans on one of them. That is the
whole reason. None of them was read, and none was filed for its merit.

- Fraenkel, *The Dual State* (1941), [LIT-805](../../record/literature.d/LIT-805.md): the normative and the
  prerogative state, and authority over whether the rules apply.
- Ashby, *Design for a Brain* (1952; the essay cites the 1960 edition),
  [LIT-787](../../record/literature.d/LIT-787.md): ultrastability, regulation against alteration of the
  parameters of regulation.
- Canguilhem, *On the Normal and the Pathological* (1943; English 1978,
  reissued by Zone Books in 1989), [LIT-817](../../record/literature.d/LIT-817.md): health as a capacity to
  change norms. The essay uses it interpretively.
- Craver, *Explaining the Brain* (2007), [LIT-832](../../record/literature.d/LIT-832.md): constitutive against
  causal relevance, and mechanistic explanation.

## How deeply

Registered only. Each entry is `Deferred` and says in its body that it was
written from secondary description: Crossref's records and chapter lists,
the publisher's abstract (Fraenkel), library catalogues (Canguilhem) and
reviews (Craver). No NOTE or THEORY was filed.

## Choices worth knowing

- **Dates.** `published:` is the first appearance, as in [LIT-738](../../record/literature.d/LIT-738.md): 1941
  for Fraenkel (the English edition is the first publication), 1952 for
  Ashby, 1943 for Canguilhem's thesis. None of these has a known day, so
  each is the first of January. Craver's is Crossref's 2007-06-07.
- **DOIs are of later editions** where the first has none: Oxford's 2017
  reissue of Fraenkel, Springer's digitization of Ashby's 1960 edition,
  and Reidel's 1978 translation of Canguilhem. Canguilhem's title follows
  that DOI (*On the Normal and the Pathological*), not Zone's.
- **Tags.** Ashby has no cybernetics word in the vocabulary; he is filed
  under complex-systems, as Beer's Viable System Model works are, with
  behavioral-integration for the feedback-control reading of adaptation.
  Canguilhem is filed under philosophy-of-biology, since his question is
  what biological norms are; psychopathology-and-treatment was not used,
  because the book is about disease in general, not mental disorder.

## Boundary

None is held in the Anthology of the SOTA, and no anthology topic could
hold them: they are political and legal theory, cybernetics, philosophy of
medicine and philosophy of neuroscience. A grep of the anthology's record
for the authors, titles and DOIs found no entry.

The owner gave the reference list of their working manuscript (October

Two of the 24:

Twenty-two works. They were first filed without a reading. The owner then
corrected the word: in this record, registering a work means reading it and
filing a NOTE, with THEORY documents where the reading warrants them. So the
same day each work was read where a lawful full text could be reached (see

- **Language, discourse and translation:** Saussure ([LIT-774](../../record/literature.d/LIT-774.md)), Austin
  ([LIT-785](../../record/literature.d/LIT-785.md)), Goffman's *Forms of Talk* ([LIT-780](../../record/literature.d/LIT-780.md)), Du Bois's stance
  triangle ([LIT-779](../../record/literature.d/LIT-779.md)), Gutt's *Translation and Relevance*
  ([LIT-784](../../record/literature.d/LIT-784.md)), and Hofstadter's *Le Ton beau de Marot* ([LIT-766](../../record/literature.d/LIT-766.md)).
- **Transmission and memory:** Bartlett's *Remembering* ([LIT-768](../../record/literature.d/LIT-768.md)),
  Lévi-Strauss's *Structural Anthropology* ([LIT-775](../../record/literature.d/LIT-775.md)), Griffiths and
  Kalish on iterated learning ([LIT-769](../../record/literature.d/LIT-769.md)), and Kirby, Cornish and Smith's
  laboratory iterated learning ([LIT-771](../../record/literature.d/LIT-771.md)).
- **Compositional text-to-image generation:** GenEval ([LIT-782](../../record/literature.d/LIT-782.md)),
  T2I-CompBench ([LIT-783](../../record/literature.d/LIT-783.md)), Composable Diffusion ([LIT-770](../../record/literature.d/LIT-770.md)), and Shi
  and colleagues' conditional diffusion Schrödinger bridges ([LIT-776](../../record/literature.d/LIT-776.md)).

## The boundary

None of the 22 is held in the Anthology of the SOTA. I grepped a clone of
its record/ taken 2026-10-09 (commit 1cffe8f) for every author, arXiv id and
title. GenEval and T2I-CompBench are named there only in prose inside other
entries, and the rest are not named at all.

The four text-to-image works are machine-learning papers. The anthology's
`generative-modeling` and `analysis-and-evaluation` topics could hold them,
so by default they belong there. They are filed here because the owner asked
for the manuscript's references to be filed in this record. Each carries
`anthology-candidate` last ([ADR-005](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-005.md)), which leaves the move to a later
decision.

They were first tagged with the nearest words this vocabulary had, and the
readings found those words did not fit. `compositionality` now holds GenEval,
T2I-CompBench and Composable Diffusion ([ADR-031](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-031.md)). The conditional
Schrödinger bridge stays under `probabilistic-modeling` and `mathematics`,
and its reader judged those tags defensible. No word for generative
modelling was added. That is the anthology's subject.

The other works fit existing words. Blackwell and Torgersen are the
exception, and they moved to `mathematical-statistics` ([ADR-031](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-031.md)).
`linguistics` is a loose fit for the two translation books, Gutt and
Hofstadter. A `translation` word waits until one of them has been read.

## How deeply

Nine readers worked in parallel, one per group, under a common brief. The
brief required a lawful full text, a reading on the work's own merits
without the manuscript, honesty about depth, and no NOTE where no copy
could be reached. Thirteen works now have a NOTE and are Active:

- **Read:** Shannon ([NOTE-591](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md)), Blackwell ([NOTE-595](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md)), Fritz
  ([NOTE-588](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md)), Baez and Fong ([NOTE-598](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-598.md)), Dzhafarov and Kujala
  ([NOTE-600](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-600.md)), GenEval ([NOTE-593](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-593.md)), T2I-CompBench ([NOTE-592](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-592.md)),
  Composable Diffusion ([NOTE-597](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-597.md)), conditional Schrödinger bridges
  ([NOTE-589](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md)), Griffiths and Kalish ([NOTE-599](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-599.md)), Saussure
  ([NOTE-594](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-594.md)), and Du Bois ([NOTE-590](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-590.md)).
- **Skimmed:** Kirby, Cornish and Smith ([NOTE-596](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-596.md)). PNAS, PubMed Central
  and the Edinburgh repository all refused this client. The reading went
  through a fetch tool that paraphrases, and its NOTE says so.

Nine works are still Deferred, now worded "filed, not read". Each LIT lists
the sources tried and what they returned. Most of these are books still in
copyright, which the Internet Archive lends but does not show and
HathiTrust searches but does not show: Austin, Goffman, Hofstadter, Gutt,
Lévi-Strauss, Bartlett, Cover and Thomas, and Torgersen. Wyner and Ziv is
an IEEE article with no repository copy.

Points the readers raised:

- **Sources worth noting.**
  - Saussure was read in French from Wikisource. That text follows the 1931
    third edition, because no scan of the 1916 edition was reachable.
  - Blackwell was read from page images on Project Euclid.
  - Du Bois was read from his own upload of the chapter, through a Wayback
    Machine capture, because ResearchGate refused the request.
  - Shannon was read from the Harvard posting of the corrected reprint.
- **Corrections to what was first filed from abstracts.**
  - Blackwell 1953 does not contain the whole "more informative iff garbling"
    equivalence. Part is Blackwell 1951 and part is Sherman and Stein. The
    1953 paper extends it to arbitrary outcome spaces and adds the
    two-state result.
  - Saussure says a sign as a whole is "un fait positif". Only signifier and
    signified, taken separately, are purely differential.
  - In Kirby, Cornish and Smith, compositional structure appeared only under
    the experimenter's homonym filter. Without it, the languages collapsed.
  - Composable Diffusion loses to its baseline at composing relations.
- **Claims the papers' own tables contradict.** The NOTEs record these.
  - CDSB: "lowest error consistently" in filtering.
  - T2I-CompBench: GORS's drop on unseen pairs, which the paper calls
    "slightly lower".
- **A finding against an older entry.** [LIT-317](../../record/literature.d/LIT-317.md) credits Shannon's 1949
  paper with the sampling theorem and the Gaussian capacity formula. Both
  are already in the 1948 paper. [NOTE-591](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md) reports this, and [LIT-317](../../record/literature.d/LIT-317.md) is
  left for its own reading to correct.
- **Options for the owner.** Each of these is a separate work that could be
  filed on its own if wanted:
  - Goffman's "Footing" (Semiotica 1979), once a copy is supplied;
  - Lévi-Strauss's "The Structural Study of Myth" (Journal of American
    Folklore 1955);
  - Gutt's 1989 thesis.

THEORY: five new, all Proposed:

- [THEORY-156](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), Blackwell's comparison of experiments;
- [THEORY-157](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md), the sufficiency theorems in Markov categories;
- [THEORY-158](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-158.md), Noether for Markov processes;
- [THEORY-159](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md), linguistic value;
- [THEORY-155](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md), iterated learning converges to the prior.

One existing THEORY changed. [THEORY-014](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-014.md) gains Contextuality-by-Default as a
third instance of its signed-solution pattern, and the claim itself is
unchanged.

Two readers reported gaps in the vocabulary independently, and the owner
authorised extending it. `compositionality` and `mathematical-statistics`
join the topics by [ADR-031](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-031.md).

## What a reading should check

These entries deliberately say nothing about the manuscript. The owner wants
each work read first on its own merits, so that the reading is not tilted by
the use the owner expects to make of it. So a reading of any of these works
answers what the work itself establishes, and leaves the manuscript out. How
a work serves the manuscript is a later and separate question.

The four text-to-image works have been read, and the move to the anthology
can now be decided on what they are. Each NOTE marks the ML-practice content
in it as anthology material. The CDSB filtering experiments are probabilistic
modelling outside deep learning, and they belong here whichever way the
move goes.

## How the readings bear on the argument

The coordinator added grounds and notes to the claims of the manuscript's
argument (line `pragmatic-transport`). Several readings change those claims.

- **The conceded prior art is stronger than the exchange knew.** Zhao et
  al. already formalise preserving the posterior over interpretations,
  which is the information bottleneck under KL divergence.
- **The quantum-cognition evidence counts against quantum contextuality.**
  Its strongest result, the QQ equality, counts against reading order
  effects that way, which is what the manuscript claims.
- **The Δ_CF claim needs restating.** It is undefined under signalling and
  cannot rise along free operations. Its premise that the contextual
  fraction is discontinuous is wrong within a scenario.
- **The Noether-type claim is weaker than it reads.** Baez's account puts
  the symmetry–conservation equivalence in an antisymmetric bracket, which a
  Markov kernel lacks.
- **The CbD 2.0 qualification holds, but only for binary observables.**
  The canonical-systems paper shows that the verdict depends on the
  representation.

## Points for the owner

- **Brandom was skimmed from the author's own posted course scans** of the
  whole book. The history note says so. Revert it to Deferred if that
  source is not acceptable.
- **"Frank, Goodman & Tenenbaum 2009" is ambiguous.** The paper registered
  is the word-learning paper. The informative-speaker precursor of rational
  speech acts is Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum 2009 (CogSci), which is
  not held.
- **Gogioso and Pinzani's successor** (arXiv 2206.08911) is not held. If it
  is filed, the withdrawn paper becomes Superseded by it.
- **One reader sent the owner's email address to Unpaywall** in a single API
  query. It was not repeated, and the other readers were told not to send it.

## Follow-up, same day

At the owner's request, two more works were registered:

- **Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum 2009** ([LIT-824](../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md), read): the
  informative-speaker precursor of rational speech acts. It confirms that
  the informative speaker is in this paper, not in the word-learning paper
  of the same year.
- **The successors to Gogioso and Pinzani.** These are the three papers into
  which "The Topology and Geometry of Causality" was split: Combinatorics
  ([LIT-800](../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md)), Topology ([LIT-808](../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md)) and Geometry ([LIT-788](../../record/literature.d/LIT-788.md)). All
  three are read, Geometry skimmed. The withdrawn paper is now Superseded by
  them, and [THEORY-171](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) gives the sheaf condition for causal functions.

The vocabulary still has no word for causal structure. Those works are
tagged by their sheaf and contextuality content.

Later the same day, at the owner's request, `causality` joined the topics
([ADR-035](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-035.md)). It goes first on the causal-order works, and it is added beside
the existing tags on the record's other works about causation.

<a id="20261009181825"></a>

## Five papers on the theory of trained networks

*2026-10-09 18:18:25 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-180 THEORY-182 THEORY-181 THEORY-022 — Proposed; cited as what this batch filed or bears on -->

The owner gave five arXiv papers to register, with no stated context. Each
was read on its own merits by a separate reader, from the arXiv PDF, and
each now has an Active LIT and a Read NOTE. All five fall on one theme:
what can be solved or measured about how networks train and what their
weights hold.

## What entered

- **Single-head attention in high dimensions** (Boncoraglio et al.,
  [LIT-857](../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md)), with a Proposed THEORY ([THEORY-180](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md)): weight decay on
  tied query–key weights is exactly a nuclear-norm penalty on their
  product. The spectral law that follows is derived, not proved; the paper
  calls its main results "Claims".
- **Closed-form dynamics of word2vec-like models** (Karkada, Simon, Bahri &
  DeWeese, [LIT-855](../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md)), with a Proposed THEORY ([THEORY-182](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)): a
  rank-limited contrastive embedding learns the top eigenvectors of the
  co-occurrence deviation one at a time, not the best low-rank PMI. Proved
  for a proxy of word2vec, not word2vec.
- **Exact learning dynamics of in-context learning in linear transformers**
  (Mainali & Teixeira, [LIT-859](../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md)). No THEORY: a Saxe-style solution whose
  fixed point was already known; its non-linear half rests on timing
  coincidences.
- **Towards understanding grokking** (Liu et al., [LIT-858](../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md)), with a
  Proposed THEORY ([THEORY-181](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md)) on when a training set fixes the
  generalising representation in the toy model.
- **Small singular values matter** (Staats, Thamm & Rosenow, [LIT-856](../../record/literature.d/LIT-856.md)).
  No THEORY. Its claim that information sits in the lower outliers of the
  spectrum is inferred from decile ablations that do not isolate them.

## The boundary

Four are not held in the anthology clone (commit d8b5ba5, possibly stale)
and carry `anthology-candidate`. The fifth, Staats et al., is held there as
[ANTH-LIT-517](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-517.md) with its reading [ANTH-NOTE-263](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/notes.d/NOTE-263.md), and is held here too under
[ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md). The second question here is how far a random-matrix null can
locate information in a learned matrix. The reading here disagrees with
[ANTH-NOTE-263](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/notes.d/NOTE-263.md) on one point (the Llama key and value exception), recorded in
its NOTE and not corrected there.

## Found along the way

- Three of the five changed title between arXiv versions; each LIT uses the
  current title and records the earlier one.
- Boncoraglio et al. cite Staats et al. as their empirical source for
  transformer weight spectra.
- Liu et al. is the earliest work in the record to find the circle in
  modular-addition embeddings, which [THEORY-022](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-022.md) is about. Adding it to that
  THEORY's sources is left to a revision of [THEORY-022](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-022.md).
- The vocabulary has no word for training dynamics, random-matrix theory or
  distributional semantics. `learning-theory` stands in loosely. No word was
  added.
- The owner ruled the same day that, when sources disagree on a date, the
  earlier one is taken ([ADR-002](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md), version 2).

## Thirteen works on hierarchy and hyperbolic geometry

*2026-10-09 20:36:09 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: QUESTION-025 THEORY-195 THEORY-188 THEORY-196 THEORY-192 THEORY-189 THEORY-193 THEORY-191 THEORY-194 THEORY-190 — Proposed or open; cited as what this batch filed or bears on -->

Right after [QUESTION-025](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-025.md) was opened (do correlated or hierarchical attributes
in co-occurrence still give linear attribute directions, and a non-Boolean
concept lattice?), the owner asked for six works, then a seventh, then six
more by link. Each was read on its own merits by a separate reader, and each
has an Active LIT and a Read NOTE. Where the owner gave only an author and a
year, or only a link, the reader confirmed the work before filing.

## What entered

**Hierarchy in learning and data.**
- Cagnetta et al., the random hierarchy model ([LIT-877](../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md)), with
  [THEORY-195](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md) on the sample complexity of learning hierarchical data.
- Larsson, Maity & Tsiotras 2022 ([LIT-868](../../record/literature.d/LIT-868.md)), information-theoretic
  pruning of a given quadtree. No THEORY; despite its title, no hierarchy
  emerges.

**Hyperbolic geometry of networks.**
- Krioukov et al. 2010 ([LIT-865](../../record/literature.d/LIT-865.md)), with [THEORY-188](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-188.md) stating the
  model result only.
- Bianconi & Rahmede 2017 ([LIT-867](../../record/literature.d/LIT-867.md)), with [THEORY-193](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-193.md): the
  curvature comes from an equal-length convention, not from the growth.
- García-Pérez, Boguñá & Serrano 2018 ([LIT-869](../../record/literature.d/LIT-869.md)), with [THEORY-190](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-190.md):
  the network model is approximately closed under geometric
  coarse-graining.

**Hyperbolic embeddings in machine learning.**
- Sala, De Sa, Gu & Ré 2018 ([LIT-874](../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md)), with [THEORY-196](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-196.md) on the
  precision cost of tree embeddings.
- Ganea, Bécigneul & Hofmann 2018 ([LIT-866](../../record/literature.d/LIT-866.md)), with [THEORY-189](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-189.md) on
  entailment cones; their transitivity is asserted, not proved.
- Lin, Coifman, Mishne & Talmon 2023 ([LIT-870](../../record/literature.d/LIT-870.md)). No THEORY; the reader
  found a gap in one proof step.
- Yang et al. 2023 ([LIT-871](../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md)). No THEORY; trained hyperbolic models do
  not place tree levels by radius on their own.

**Hyperbolic geometry in brains and perception.**
- Zhou, Smith & Sharpee 2018 ([LIT-872](../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md)), with [THEORY-191](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md) on the
  olfactory space.
- Zhang, Rich, Lee & Sharpee 2022 ([LIT-876](../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md)), with [THEORY-192](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md) on
  the hippocampus.
- Sharpee 2019 ([LIT-875](../../record/literature.d/LIT-875.md)), a perspective. No THEORY; its argument from
  Zipf's law is an analogy.

**Renormalization and information.**
- Koch-Janusz & Ringel 2018 ([LIT-873](../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md)), with [THEORY-194](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md): the
  coarse-graining that stays informative about the environment is the
  relevant one. It shares a Nature Physics issue with García-Pérez et al.
  but is not a companion paper.

## Bearing on [QUESTION-025](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-025.md)

None answers it; their bearings are written into the question's new
section. The nearest thing to an answer was already in the record: Saxe et
al. 2019 ([LIT-862](../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md)) gives tree-shaped linear directions for hierarchical
features in a linear network, one per branching rather than one per
attribute. The batch adds that hierarchy may be held by distances or by
containment rather than directions, that hyperbolic curvature alone is not
evidence of hierarchy, and that none of the geometric encodings gives a
lattice's meets and joins.

## The boundary

None is held in the anthology clone (commit d8b5ba5, possibly stale). The
machine-learning papers (Cagnetta, Sala, Ganea, Lin, Yang, Koch-Janusz &
Ringel) carry `anthology-candidate`; the network, neuroscience and
information-theory papers do not.

## Found along the way

- Several readers reported no word for hyperbolic or metric geometry, for
  statistical physics and the renormalization group, or for perception.
  `mathematics`, `network-science`, `natural-sciences` and `cognition`
  stand in. No word was added.
- The olfaction paper's date is its online date, 29 August 2018, not the
  issue's cover date of 3 August, which predates the article. The
  earlier-date rule settles real doubt about first appearance; a cover
  date before the article existed is not one.
- Works these papers build on that neither record holds: three follow-ups
  to the random hierarchy model (arXiv 2402.16991, 2404.10727,
  2406.00048); Koch-Janusz & Ringel's sequels (arXiv 1809.09632,
  2101.11633) and Mehta & Schwab (arXiv 1410.3831), which they argue
  against; Ganea et al.'s *Hyperbolic Neural Networks* (NeurIPS 2018).
